ambiguities.text: The specification does not define what clients should do if they encounter an empty account in post-merge state (e.g., crash, ignore, clean up).
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume clients should treat this as a critical error condition since behavior is undefined. Implementation may vary but the state is considered invalid.

ambiguities.text: The phrase 'specification is undefined' could mean the behavior is implementation-specific or that it should never occur.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume it means the condition should never occur in a valid post-merge network, and any occurrence indicates a bug or attack.

ambiguities.text: The mechanism by which empty accounts were 'cleared prior to the merge' on mainnet is not specified in this EIP.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume this refers to the Spurious Dragon cleanup and subsequent state pruning that occurred during earlier hard forks.

implicit_assumptions.description: The claim that 'all empty accounts on Ethereum Mainnet were cleared prior to the merge' is accurate and verifiable.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Empty accounts in mainnet post-merge state could cause client bugs, consensus issues, or undefined behavior.

implicit_assumptions.description: The Spurious Dragon fork correctly prevents creation of new empty accounts through its state clearing mechanism.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: New empty accounts could be created, violating the post-merge invariant.

implicit_assumptions.description: All test cases and tooling will be updated to not include post-merge empty accounts.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Invalid test cases could pass, masking bugs in empty account handling.

implicit_assumptions.description: An attacker cannot craft transactions that leave accounts in an empty state post-merge.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Attacker could deliberately create undefined behavior states in clients.
